item.title: HyperPod InstantStart launched to simplify Amazon SageMaker HyperPod cluster composition
item.description:
HyperPod InstantStart launched to simplify Amazon SageMaker HyperPod cluster composition

Running foundation model (FM) workloads on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod is a chain of dependent tasks rather than a single action. Infrastructure teams must create the network and control plane, attach accelerator capacity, install cluster dependencies, prepare storage and identity, and deploy model servers. To address the operational challenges of managing these handoffs, HyperPod InstantStart has been introduced as an open-source control plane built for resource composition.

🔍 Overview

While Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) provides direct Kubernetes access as a user-managed orchestration surface, it traditionally requires teams to compose AWS resources, add-ons, workloads, and day-two operations manually. Each step has its own API, failure modes, and waiting periods.

Amazon SageMaker HyperPod reduces this operational burden by offering managed, resilient compute and Amazon EKS integrated capabilities. HyperPod InstantStart directly resolves the remaining composition challenges by automating multi-stage workflows.

🧩 How it works

HyperPod InstantStart runs as a single, out-of-band management container in your AWS account. It calls AWS service APIs and the Kubernetes API, but does not sit in the data path of your training jobs or inference requests.

The control plane offers two ways to drive its operations, both entering through the same single container:

  • AI Agent Orchestration: An AI agent plans the multi-stage workflow, launches each stage, and polls asynchronous AWS operations until completion. The agent pauses only for user-defined decisions—such as selecting the Availability Zone, instance type, and capacity type—before handing back a running cluster with storage mounted.
  • Unified Interfaces: The web UI, the REST API, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools represent three faces of the same container. Both interfaces call the same backend APIs, pass the same validations, and read the same persisted operation state, ensuring neither interface has private logic the other lacks.

Because everything created by HyperPod InstantStart is a standard AWS or Kubernetes resource, infrastructure teams can inspect all outputs directly using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and kubectl.

⚙️ Key details

The capabilities managed across AWS and Amazon SageMaker HyperPod are structured as follows:

Operational Category Managed Capabilities
Infrastructure Health monitoring, deep health checks, and automatic node recovery
Capacity Continuous provisioning and managed Karpenter autoscaling
Training Process-level recovery and managed tiered checkpointing
Inference Intelligent routing and tiered key-value (KV) caching
Storage & Registry Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), Amazon FSx for Lustre, and Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) to carry images, data, and checkpoints

#AWS #SageMaker #Kubernetes #AIagents #OpenSource

Source: Run agent-driven Amazon SageMaker HyperPod operations with InstantStart | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Fine-tuning a 350M Parameter Model for Improved Structured Output Generation
item.description:
Fine-tuning a 350M Parameter Model for Improved Structured Output Generation

A recent development demonstrates how to fine-tune a 350M parameter model to improve structured output adherence using 100 GRPO steps. The process utilizes a custom training pipeline and an accessible benchmark to test validity and schema compliance.

🔍 Overview

The project uses the IFStruct benchmark to evaluate LLM output validity. By applying fine-tuning, the model improves its ability to follow formatting instructions and schema requirements. The evaluation was conducted locally on a MacBook Pro with an Apple M5 Max and 36 GB of unified memory using llama.cpp.

🧩 How it works

The training process involves approximately 500 samples:

  • 40% of samples include an instruction to return output within a fenced code block.
  • 20% of samples are converted into top-level-array tasks to train for bare-list output and item-count compliance.

⚙️ Key details

For local execution, the setup uses the BF16 GGUF version of the LFM2.5-350M model. The server configuration includes a context size of 32768, parallel request processing of 4, and full GPU layer offloading.

Metric Result (Passed/Total) Percentage
Overall 452/2000 22.6%
JSON 180/1000 18.0%
YAML 272/1000 27.2%
Wrapper key 288/1011 28.5%
Bare list 164/989 16.6%

🚀 Availability

The IFStruct benchmark is open-source and available via Liquid4All/ifstruct. The public benchmark dataset is hosted on Hugging Face at LiquidAI/ifstruct-v1.0.

#AI #LLM #OpenSource #MachineLearning

Source: Fine-tuning a 350M Model for Better Structured Outputs in 100 GRPO Steps

item.title: Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion
item.description:
Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion

Nvidia has agreed to purchase Hugging Face, the popular open-source AI platform, for $12.93 billion.

🔍 Overview

  • Hugging Face is an online platform founded in 2016 that hosts open-source AI models, datasets, and tools.
  • It is often described as the “GitHub” for AI due to its browsable library and community collaboration features.

⚙️ Key details

  • The acquisition price is $12.93 billion, nearly triple Hugging Face’s last valuation of $4.5 billion in 2023.
  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated: “Together, we will scale Hugging Face’s platform, strengthen its infrastructure and expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide.”
  • Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem.
  • Developers will retain the choice of models, frameworks, clouds, inference service providers, and computing platforms.
  • Nvidia compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face.

📅 Timeline

  • Speculation began on August 23rd after reports that Hugging Face was exploring a $13 billion sale.
  • By August 27th, reports indicated Nvidia was in acquisition talks with Hugging Face, with earlier claims of a $12.9 billion deal already agreed upon.
  • Nvidia has now publicly declared its intent to purchase Hugging Face.

💡 Why it matters

  • Nvidia gains a strategic foothold to help preserve its AI hardware dominance as closed-source AI providers develop their own chips.
  • Hugging Face previously rejected a $500 million investment offer from Nvidia in 2023, which would have valued it at $7 billion.
  • Hugging Face generates around $150 million in annualized revenue, a fraction of its purchase price.

#Nvidia #HuggingFace #AI #acquisition #open-source #AIhardware

Source: Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for almost $13 billion

item.title: Open-source AI paints watercolors by writing JavaScript code
item.description:
Open-source AI paints watercolors by writing JavaScript code

On 23 August Surya Narreddi posted a beautiful video of watercolour paintings generated by a language model that writes JavaScript through p5.brush, a library that adds natural drawing tools to p5.js. The video went viral fast, with over 1.5 M views at the time of writing.

🔍 Overview

  • The model generates a program of about 150 lines of JavaScript that paints the image.
  • Output is code, which can be read, edited, and re‑run; the decision behind each brushstroke is visible.
  • Style is shaped by a restriction to only ten methods of the p5.brush library.
  • The resulting paintings look loose, imperfect, and handmade, contrasting with the statistically‑average pictures of typical image models.

🛠️ How it works

  • Training data: a hand‑rated pool of reference images (initially close‑up flowers, later full compositions).
  • Reward design: uses the same framing as the original blog; three reward mixes were trained and compared.
  • Reinforcement‑learning stack: built with TRL and OpenEnv; the RL environment is provided in the repository.
  • Execution: the generated JavaScript runs in p5.js via the p5.brush library, producing the final watercolor rendering.

📦 Open implementation

  • The author reproduced the idea step‑by‑step, publishing:
    • Reference‑pool dataset
    • RL environment
    • Training scripts
    • Trained models
  • All artifacts are open‑source; once two Hugging Face Spaces are up, the entire pipeline runs with a single command.
  • The repository includes a “What I would try next” list that captures ideas not incorporated into the experiments.

💡 Why it matters

  • The project revives the early generative‑AI‑art mindset where the medium and exploration were central, echoing works such as DeepDream (2015), Edmond de Belamy (2018), and the portraits of Mario Klingemann.
  • By outputting editable code instead of a static image, the approach offers transparency and creative control.
  • The viral response (over 1.5 M views) indicates strong public interest in AI‑generated art that retains a handcrafted aesthetic.

Surya’s site notes that a full technical report is forthcoming.

#AIart #RL #OpenSource #p5js #GenerativeArt

Source: Training a coding model to paint watercolours with TRL and OpenEnv

item.title: text2ql Enables Multi-Target Natural Language Database Queries with Deterministic Mode
item.description:
text2ql Enables Multi-Target Natural Language Database Queries with Deterministic Mode

A new open‑source Python framework called text2ql was submitted on 2 Sep 2026. It targets natural‑language interfaces to databases and claims to overcome three common structural limitations.

🔍 Overview

  • Addresses exclusive focus on relational SQL, mandatory reliance on large‑language‑model (LLM) inference at query time, and lack of runtime signals for semantically incorrect queries.
  • Introduces a language‑agnostic Intermediate Representation named QueryIR and a pluggable renderer architecture.

🧩 How it works

  • A single seven‑stage detection pipeline can generate queries for both SQL and GraphQL targets.
  • Supports two operating modes:
    1. LLM‑backed mode – leverages an LLM to interpret natural language.
    2. Zero‑LLM deterministic mode – bypasses LLM inference entirely.
  • Every generated query is accompanied by a runtime confidence score ranging from 0.15 to 0.97, computed via an additive signal model.

⚙️ Key details

  • Performance (LLM‑backed mode) on 50‑query random samples from the Spider and BIRD benchmarks:
    • Exact‑match accuracy: 62 %–70 %
    • Execution accuracy: 84 %–91 %
  • Performance (Deterministic mode) on 100 test cases:
    • Execution accuracy: 100 % with zero parse errors
    • Median latency: 3.2 ms
    • No API cost (zero‑LLM)
  • Ablation study shows schema‑aware prompting adds +18.4 percentage points to exact‑match performance compared with a schema‑free baseline.
Mode Exact Match Execution Accuracy Median Latency API Cost
LLM‑backed 62 %–70 % 84 %–91 % – –
Deterministic (zero‑LLM) – 100 % 3.2 ms None

🚀 Availability

  • text2ql is released as open‑source under the Apache 2.0 license.
  • Implemented in Python and designed to be language‑agnostic via the QueryIR.

💡 Why it matters

  • By providing a deterministic, zero‑LLM option, text2ql eliminates inference latency and API costs while guaranteeing execution correctness.
  • The runtime confidence scores give developers immediate feedback on query reliability.
  • Supporting both SQL and GraphQL expands applicability across relational and graph databases.

#text2ql #NL2SQL #open-source #databases #AI

Source: text2ql: Multi-Target Natural Language Querying via a Language-Agnostic Intermediate Representation

item.title: Python 3.15.0 Release Candidate 2 Announced Ahead of October Launch
item.description:
Python 3.15.0 Release Candidate 2 Announced Ahead of October Launch

Hugo van Kemenade, the release manager for Python 3.14 and 3.15, has announced the release of Python 3.15.0 candidate 2. This version represents the final release candidate phase before the official launch of Python 3.15.0 scheduled for October.

🔍 Overview

With the transition into the release candidate phase, the development process is now restricted. Only reviewed code changes that qualify as clear bug fixes are allowed between this release candidate and the final stable release.

⚙️ Key details

  • Binary Compatibility: Any binary wheels built against Python 3.15.0 release candidates will work with all future versions of Python 3.15.
  • Maintainer Action: Maintainers of third-party projects are strongly encouraged to prepare for the 3.15 release and publish wheels on PyPI now to assist other projects with their testing.
  • Bug Mitigation: Testing during the RC period helps prevent shipping bugs in the final release, a lesson learned by developers who have discovered bugs in previous versions, such as Python 3.10, only after they had already shipped.

🧩 How it works

While the new RC is not yet available directly for GitHub Actions via actions/python-versions, developers can test against it by configuring their testing matrix as follows:

1
2
3
4
5
6
7
8
9

strategy:
 matrix:
 python-version: ["3.14", "3.15"]
steps:
 - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
 with:
 python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
 allow-prereleases: true
 check-latest: true

The allow-prereleases and check-latest flags ensure that the workflow automatically tests against the latest candidate (switching from RC1 to RC2 as they land) and eventually the stable version once it is released.

🚀 Availability

The final release of Python 3.15.0 is expected in October. Developers and maintainers are encouraged to utilize the current RC2 phase to ensure their projects are ready for the final launch.

item.title: CrewAI introduces open-source multi-agent framework and AMP Suite
item.description:
CrewAI introduces open-source multi-agent framework and AMP Suite

CrewAI has launched an open-source Python framework for building production-ready multi-agent workflows, alongside the CrewAI AMP Suite for enterprise-grade deployment and management.

🔍 Overview

CrewAI is an open-source Python framework designed to enable autonomous agent collaboration through Crews and precise, event-driven control through Flows. It fosters collaborative intelligence, allowing agents to work together seamlessly on complex tasks.

🧩 How it works

  • Crews: Optimize for autonomy and collaborative intelligence with role-based AI agents.
  • Flows: Build event-driven automations combining precise workflow control, single LLM calls, and native support for Crews.
  • High-level abstractions and low-level APIs: Provides flexibility for developers to build production-ready multi-agent systems.

⚙️ Key details

CrewAI offers:

  • Role-based AI agents with defined goals, backstories, and tools.
  • Structured task descriptions and dependencies for workflow automation.
  • Community-driven learning with over 100,000 developers certified through courses at learn.crewai.com.

The CrewAI AMP Suite adds:

  • Managed deployment, observability, governance, security, and enterprise support.
  • Crew Control Plane with key features:
    • Tracing & Observability: Real-time monitoring of agents and workflows, including metrics, logs, and traces.
    • Unified Control Plane: Centralized platform for managing, monitoring, and scaling AI agents and workflows.
    • Seamless Integrations: Connectivity with existing enterprise systems, data sources, and cloud infrastructure.
    • Advanced Security: Robust security and compliance measures.
    • Actionable Insights: Real-time analytics and reporting.
    • 24/7 Support: Dedicated enterprise support.
    • On-premise and Cloud Deployment Options: Flexible deployment based on security and compliance requirements.

🚀 Availability

  • The CrewAI framework is open-source and available for developers.
  • The Crew Control Plane, part of the AMP Suite, is available for free trial.
  • CrewAI AMP Suite is designed for enterprises seeking scalable, intelligent automation solutions.

💡 Why it matters

CrewAI is rapidly becoming the standard for production-ready agentic automation, offering both a flexible open-source framework and an enterprise-grade suite for managed deployment and control.

item.title: Debian Project Approves New Policy Allowing Generative AI in Linux Development
item.description:
Debian Project Approves New Policy Allowing Generative AI in Linux Development

The Debian Project has voted to allow developers to use AI tools in their contributions to the Linux distribution’s development, maintenance, and documentation. The new policy acknowledges that the responsible use of AI can improve productivity while clarifying that the project neither endorses nor prohibits the use of generative AI tools.

🔍 Overview

The decision follows a vote by project developers who considered several other proposals, including options that would have banned contributions made using AI tools. Under the new policy, generative AI is neither exempt from nor subject to special rules beyond the standards already expected of Debian contributors.

⚙️ Key details

Debian has established specific guidelines for how AI-assisted work must be handled within the project:

  • Maintained Standards: All contributions must satisfy the same standards of quality, correctness, maintainability, and legal compliance, regardless of the tools used.
  • Contributor Responsibility: Using a generative AI tool does not diminish a contributor’s responsibility for the work they submit.
  • Review Requirements: Contributors are expected to understand, review, test, and modify AI-assisted output before incorporating it into the distribution.
  • Human Oversight: The project states that blindly accepting or uploading AI-generated material without human review is inconsistent with established development practices.
  • Disclosure: Debian encourages contributors to disclose if a contribution was made with AI assistance, but it does not require them to do so.

💡 Why it matters

The policy change has caused friction within the community. One contributor has indicated he is quitting the project and is no longer interested in Debian following the vote. This reaction mirrors a similar backlash faced by Ubuntu developer Canonical earlier this year regarding its own stance on AI tools.

#Debian #Linux #GenerativeAI #OpenSource

Source: Debian won’t ban AI code from its Linux distribution

item.title: DeerFlow 2.0 open-source super agent harness tops GitHub Trending
item.description:
DeerFlow 2.0 open-source super agent harness tops GitHub Trending

On February 28th, 2026, DeerFlow claimed the 🏆 #1 spot on GitHub Trending following the launch of version 2.

🔍 Overview

DeerFlow (Deep Exploration and Efficient Research Flow) is an open-source super agent harness that orchestrates sub-agents, memory, and sandboxes to perform long-horizon tasks such as research, coding, and creation.

🧩 How it works

DeerFlow handles different levels of tasks—spanning minutes to hours—using:

  • Sandboxes for isolated execution
  • Memory systems for state retention
  • Tools and skills for specialized operations
  • Subagents for modular task delegation
  • A message gateway for inter-agent communication

A desktop tool accompanies DeerFlow to prototype agent ideas, inspect each harness step, replay failures, and benchmark performance.

⚙️ Key details

DeerFlow 2.0 is a ground-up rewrite with no shared code with v1.

Supported models for running DeerFlow:

  • Doubao-Seed-2.0-Code
  • DeepSeek v3.2
  • Kimi 2.5

New integrations:

  • BytePlus–InfoQuest intelligent search and crawling toolset (supports free online experience)

Development status:

  • Active development has moved to 2.0
  • Original Deep Research framework maintained on the 1.x branch
  • Contributions to 1.x are still welcome

🚀 Availability

  • Source code: Available on GitHub
  • Setup: Clone the repo if needed, then bootstrap local development via Install.md
  • Demos: Real demos available on the official website
  • Case studies: Landing-page showcases open as allowlisted, read-only demos without sign-in

For coding agents, a one-sentence prompt can automate setup:

Help me clone DeerFlow if needed, then bootstrap it for local development by following https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bytedance/deer-flow/main/Install.md

💡 Why it matters

DeerFlow enables autonomous, multi-step workflows that extend beyond short, single-turn tasks, making it suitable for complex, long-duration projects in research and development.

#DeerFlow #AIagents #opensource #GitHubTrending #automation

Source: bytedance/deer-flow

item.title: LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation Now at v1.0+
item.description:
LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation Now at v1.0+

LightRAG is an open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system developed by the HKUDS research group. It is designed for simplicity and speed, and has recently hit a series of milestones marked as “NEW” features, indicating first-time enhancements to its core capabilities.

🧩 How it works

LightRAG operates on a graph-based approach to RAG, integrating with various storage backends and embedding services to retrieve and generate answers from a knowledge base.

⚙️ Key details

  • Multimodal Support: As of the June 2025 release, LightRAG integrates with RAG-Anything for an “All-in-One Multimodal RAG” system. This enables parsing and retrieval across diverse formats including PDFs, images, Office documents, tables, and formulas.
  • Scalability: A scalability enhancement in October 2025 eliminated processing bottlenecks to support large-scale datasets efficiently.
  • Query Performance: August 2025 updates introduced a default Reranker mode to boost performance for mixed queries and a Document Deletion feature with automatic knowledge graph regeneration.
  • Open-Source LLM Focus: In September 2025, enhancements were made to improve knowledge graph extraction accuracy for open-sourced LLMs like Qwen3-30B-A3B.
  • Observability: November 2025 integration added RAGAS for Evaluation and Langfuse for Tracing, updating the API to return retrieved contexts for context precision metrics.
  • Storage & Setup: March 2026 brought OpenSearch as a unified storage backend and a setup wizard supporting local Docker deployment for embedding, reranking, and storage services.

🚀 Availability

LightRAG is available as a Python package (lightrag-hku) on PyPI. The source code is hosted on GitHub, with community support via Discord and WeChat.

💡 Why it matters

Recent development activity shows a rapid cadence of new features focused on multimodal integration, scalability, and operational tooling, moving LightRAG from a simple framework to a more comprehensive platform for building RAG applications.

#RAG #KnowledgeGraph #AI #OpenSource #Retrieval

Source: HKUDS/LightRAG

item.title: New token-compression layer cuts AI agent bills up to 85%
item.description:
New token-compression layer cuts AI agent bills up to 85%

A new open-source compression layer for AI coding agents reduces input and output token counts by up to 85% without changing answers or agent code.

Compress tool outputs, logs, files, RAG chunks, and conversation history before they reach the LLM. The same answers are produced with 60–95% fewer tokens for JSON data and 15–20% fewer tokens for coding agents.

🔍 Overview

  • Compresses everything an AI agent reads—tool outputs, logs, RAG chunks, files, and conversation history—before it reaches the LLM.
  • Produces identical answers while using a fraction of the tokens.
  • Supports reversible compression so originals can be retrieved on demand.

🧩 How it works

  • Content-aware compressors: SmartCrusher, CodeCompressor, and Kompress-v2-base handle JSON, AST, or prose.
  • ContentRouter: Detects content type and selects the appropriate compressor.
  • CacheAligner: Detects volatile content that could invalidate provider KV cache prefixes.
  • CCR (Cache-Conscious Reversible) caching: Originals are cached locally; the LLM calls headroom_retrieve to fetch them when needed.
  • Tool schema filtering: Semantically filters irrelevant tools using an open embedding model (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) run locally on CPU.
  • History summarization: Trims stale conversation history to keep context windows efficient.
  • Output token reduction: Trims ceremony, restated code, and routine “thinking” from model responses.

⚙️ Key details

Component Description Usage
Library compress(messages) in Python or TypeScript Inline in any app
Proxy headroom proxy --port 8787 Zero code changes, any language
Agent wrap `headroom wrap claude codex
MCP server headroom_compress, headroom_retrieve, headroom_stats For any MCP client
Cross-agent memory Shared store across agents like Claude, Codex, Grok Auto-deduplication
Learning mode headroom learn Mines failed sessions, writes corrections to CLAUDE.local.md or similar files

🚀 Availability

  • Paritok gateway v1.0.0: Open-sourced proxy/middleware that turns a 4B model into a drop-in compression layer for agents like Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and OpenHands.
  • Paritok-4B-v1: Released on Hugging Face Hub with full SWE-bench Lite end-to-end evaluation.
  • Headroom: Library, proxy, and MCP server available for local-first deployment.
  • Drop-in for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenHands, and any BASE_URL agent without code changes.

💡 Why it matters

  • Token savings: Cuts input token bills from ~25% on turn one to past 85% in long, context-saturated sessions.
  • Context window efficiency: Fits ~3× more turns in the same context window.
  • Non-destructive: Nothing is permanently discarded; originals are recoverable on demand.
  • Local-first: Powered by an open-source 4B model trained on 45K real agent trajectories.
  • Prompt-cache friendly: Tool selection stays byte-stable turn-to-turn, preserving KV cache integrity.

#AItokens #AIagents #compression #codingagents #open-source

Source: headroomlabs-ai/headroom Source: Paritok-official/paritok-4b-v1

item.description:
OpenCode launches open source AI coding agent with desktop app

OpenCode, an open source coding agent, has released a new AI-powered development tool alongside a desktop application.

🔍 Overview

OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent designed to assist developers with coding tasks. It is available as both a command-line tool and a desktop application.

🧩 How it works

OpenCode includes two built-in agents that can be toggled with the Tab key:

  • build – A full-access agent for development work.
  • plan – A read-only agent for analysis and code exploration, which denies file edits by default and requests permission before running bash commands.

Additionally, OpenCode features a general subagent for complex searches and multistep tasks, invoked using @general in messages.

  • Installation paths follow this priority order:

    1. $OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR – Custom installation directory
    2. $XDG_BIN_DIR – XDG Base Directory Specification compliant path
    3. $HOME/bin – Standard user binary directory (if it exists or can be created)
    4. $HOME/.opencode/bin – Default fallback

  • Remove versions older than 0.1.x before installing.

  • Download options:

    • Directly from the releases page
    • Via the official website: opencode.ai/download

🚀 Availability

  • OpenCode is available as an open source project.
  • Contributions are welcome; see the contributing docs for guidelines.
  • Users are asked to clarify in their project READMEs if their project name includes “opencode” but is not affiliated with the OpenCode team.

💡 Why it matters

OpenCode provides developers with an accessible, open source tool for AI-assisted coding, offering both development and analysis agents to streamline workflows.

item.title: rLLM Open-Source Framework for Training Language Agents with Reinforcement Learning
item.description:
rLLM Open-Source Framework for Training Language Agents with Reinforcement Learning

rLLM is a new open-source framework designed for training language agents using reinforcement learning. It allows developers to use the same agent code for both evaluation and training by utilizing a model gateway that captures token IDs and logprobs.

🔍 Overview

rLLM provides a flexible environment for agent development and training with the following features:

  • Harness Support: Includes 10+ CLI harnesses (such as Claude Code, Codex, Terminus-2, mini-swe-agent, and opencode) and Harbor-compatible task directories.
  • Agent Integration: Users can wrap their own agents, including those built with LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, or openai.OpenAI, using @rllm.rollout.
  • Extensive Benchmarking: Integrates 60+ benchmarks across categories including math, code, MCQ, QA, search, VLM, translation, and agentic tasks (e.g., Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench, SkillsBench, AIME, MATH-500, and GPQA).
  • Simplified Evaluation: The rllm eval <name> command automatically pulls and runs benchmarks.

🧩 How it works

rLLM follows a pipeline: run your agent → collect traces → compute rewards → update the model.

During this process, the agent runs as-is. A model gateway captures LLM calls via URL-routed sessions and organizes them into a specific structure:

  • Episodes: One task
  • Trajectories: One agent run
  • Steps: One LLM call

A reward function then scores the result, and an RL algorithm updates the model weights.

⚙️ Key details

Training Backends

Backend Description
verl Distributed multi-GPU training (with vLLM/SGLang)
tinker Single-machine training (Tinker API)
fireworks Fireworks training platform

Technical Specifications

  • Supported Algorithms: GRPO, REINFORCE, RLOO, SFT, and on-policy distillation.
  • Infrastructure: Supports Docker, Daytona, Modal, or local environments, utilizing snapshot and warm-pool acceleration.
  • Requirements: Python >= 3.11.
  • Proven Results: State-of-the-art open-source results include DeepScaleR-1.5B, DeepCoder-14B, DeepSWE-32B, and FinQA-4B.

🚀 Availability

rLLM is open-source and has been adopted by industry research teams and academic labs.

#rLLM #ReinforcementLearning #AIAgents #OpenSource

item.title: OpenAudio S1-mini: Bringing Emotional Intelligence to Text-to-Speech Technology
item.description:
🎭 OpenAudio S1-mini: Bringing Emotional Intelligence to Text-to-Speech Technology

📝 Summary

Discover OpenAudio S1-mini, a groundbreaking text-to-speech model that supports 13 languages and over 50 emotional markers. This compact 0.5B parameter model delivers near-professional quality voice synthesis with remarkable accuracy. Learn how this open model is changing the accessibility landscape for content creators and developers working with speech technology.

🌐 The Revolution in Multilingual Voice Synthesis

Text-to-speech technology has evolved dramatically over the past decade, but most solutions have struggled with the natural expressiveness that makes human speech so engaging. Enter OpenAudio S1, a breakthrough TTS system that’s redefining what’s possible in the realm of synthetic speech.

The recently released OpenAudio S1-mini—a distilled version of the larger S1 model—has captured attention across the tech community for delivering exceptional speech synthesis capabilities in a remarkably efficient package. With training on more than 2 million hours of audio data spanning multiple languages, this model represents a significant leap forward in making natural-sounding speech synthesis accessible to developers worldwide.

🌍 Breaking Language Barriers with Impressive Multilingual Support

One of the most impressive aspects of OpenAudio S1-mini is its extensive language support. The model currently handles 13 languages:

  • 🇺🇸 English
  • 🇨🇳 Chinese
  • 🇯🇵 Japanese
  • 🇩🇪 German
  • 🇫🇷 French
  • 🇪🇸 Spanish
  • 🇰🇷 Korean
  • 🇦🇪 Arabic
  • 🇷🇺 Russian
  • 🇳🇱 Dutch
  • 🇮🇹 Italian
  • 🇵🇱 Polish
  • 🇵🇹 Portuguese

This multilingual capability makes it an invaluable tool for global applications, content localization, and accessibility improvements across linguistic boundaries. For developers working on international products, this eliminates the need to integrate multiple language-specific TTS solutions.

🎭 Beyond Words: Emotional Intelligence in Synthetic Speech

What truly sets OpenAudio S1-mini apart is its extensive support for emotional and tonal variation—a feature that’s been notoriously difficult to implement in TTS systems. The model supports an impressive array of emotional markers that can transform flat text into expressive speech:

😀 Emotional Spectrum

The S1-mini can express over 50 distinct emotional states, including:

  • 😡 Angry, furious, frustrated
  • 😢 Sad, depressed, painful
  • 😲 Surprised, astonished, excited
  • 😌 Satisfied, relaxed, confident
  • 😰 Anxious, worried, nervous
  • 😄 Delighted, joyful, amused

🔊 Vocal Tone Control

Beyond emotions, the system supports special tone markers:

  • 🏃‍♂️ “in a hurry tone”
  • 📢 “shouting”
  • 😱 “screaming”
  • 🤫 “whispering”
  • 🗣️ “soft tone”

🎭 Special Expression Markers

The model even handles paralinguistic expressions:

  • 😂 “laughing” (Ha,ha,ha)
  • 😏 “chuckling” (Hmm,hmm)
  • 😭 “sobbing” and “crying loudly”
  • 😮‍💨 “sighing”
  • 😰 “panting”

This emotional intelligence layer transforms the TTS experience from merely functional to truly communicative, enabling applications that can convey not just information but also sentiment and context.

🧠 Technical Performance: Small Package, Powerful Results

Despite being significantly smaller than its full-sized counterpart, OpenAudio S1-mini delivers impressive performance metrics that rival much larger models:

📊 Performance Metrics (English, auto-evaluated)

Metric S1 (4B) S1-mini (0.5B)
WER (Word Error Rate) 0.008 0.011
CER (Character Error Rate) 0.004 0.005
Speaker Distance 0.332 0.380

These numbers reveal that S1-mini maintains near-parity with the larger S1 model despite being approximately 8x smaller (0.5B parameters versus 4B). This efficiency is particularly noteworthy because it makes high-quality TTS accessible on more modest hardware configurations.

The implementation of online Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has clearly paid dividends in both models, contributing to their natural-sounding outputs and high accuracy rates.

🚀 Practical Applications and Access

The applications for such a capable TTS system span numerous industries:

  • 🎮 Game developers can create more dynamic NPC interactions
  • 📱 Accessibility tools can provide more natural-sounding assistance
  • 🎬 Content creators can automate voiceovers with appropriate emotional context
  • 📚 Educational platforms can deliver more engaging audio content
  • 🤖 Voice assistants can communicate with greater nuance

OpenAudio S1-mini is released under the CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 license, making it accessible for non-commercial applications while preserving attribution requirements. Developers interested in testing the model can access a demo through the Fish Audio Playground, while the full technical documentation is available on the OpenAudio website and Fish Speech GitHub repository.

💭 The Future of Voice Synthesis

The impressive capabilities of OpenAudio S1-mini highlight how rapidly TTS technology is advancing. As models become more efficient while maintaining high quality, we’re approaching a future where synthetic speech is virtually indistinguishable from human speech—not just in pronunciation accuracy, but in emotional resonance.

What makes this development particularly exciting is the democratization of advanced voice technology. By compressing sophisticated capabilities into a more compact model, OpenAudio is making these tools accessible to a wider range of developers and use cases.

The question now becomes: how will we responsibly integrate increasingly human-like synthetic voices into our digital ecosystem, and what new applications will emerge when emotional expressiveness becomes a standard feature of TTS technology?

item.title: 🚀 The Common Pile v0.1: How Open-Licensed Data is Revolutionizing LLM Training
item.description:
🚀 The Common Pile v0.1: How Open-Licensed Data is Revolutionizing LLM Training

𝗜𝗻 𝗮 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱 𝗼𝗳 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗹𝘆 𝗼𝗽𝗮𝗾𝘂𝗲 𝗔𝗜 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮, 𝗘𝗹𝗲𝘂𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗔𝗜 𝗿𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗮𝗻 𝟴 𝗧𝗕 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗲𝘅𝗶𝘀𝘁.

Introduction

Four and a half years after their groundbreaking release of the Pile, EleutherAI has done it again. 🎉 The Common Pile v0.1 represents something increasingly rare in today’s AI landscape: a massive, meticulously curated training dataset that’s fully available to researchers and developers everywhere. In collaboration with powerhouse institutions including the University of Toronto, Hugging Face, AI2, and several prestigious universities, this 8 TB corpus of openly licensed and public domain text sets a new standard for transparent AI development.

But what makes this release truly remarkable isn’t just its size—it’s what it represents in an era where AI training data has become increasingly secretive.

🧠 Why Open Training Data Matters Now More Than Ever

In recent years, we’ve witnessed a troubling trend. Even organizations once known for relative transparency like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind have dramatically scaled back disclosures about their training data. While lawsuits haven’t meaningfully changed actual data collection practices, they’ve driven the industry underground when it comes to transparency.

This opacity creates serious problems:

  • 🔬 Scientific research suffers: Studies on memorization, privacy, bias, and training dynamics become nearly impossible without access to training data
  • 🔄 Duplicated efforts: Teams waste resources recreating similar datasets rather than building upon shared foundations
  • ⚠️ Trust issues: When models are evaluated on potentially contaminated benchmarks, how can we verify results without seeing the training data?

𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘊𝘰𝘮𝘮𝘰𝘯 𝘗𝘪𝘭𝘦 offers a counter to this trend, providing a foundation for reproducible research and meaningful model comparisons.

🔍 What “Open” Really Means in AI Training Data

Creating an openly licensed dataset is far more complex than it might appear. The EleutherAI team navigated a complex legal landscape to establish clear standards for what qualifies as “open” for LLM training purposes.

Their approach aligns with established definitions from organizations like the Open Knowledge Foundation, Creative Commons, and Wikimedia: “open” grants permission to use, study, modify, and redistribute by anyone for any purpose.

The challenges they faced were substantial:

  • 🧩 Identifying licenses automatically proved unreliable in most cases
  • 📚 Public domain works are especially difficult to verify across jurisdictions
  • 🔄 License information is often buried in metadata or website fine print

One notable exception was code repositories, where tools from the Software Heritage Foundation and BigCode project enabled reliable license identification, making the openly licensed subset of Stack v2 particularly valuable to ML researchers.

🔥 Performance: Busting the “Closed Data Is Better” Myth

Perhaps the most compelling part of this release is how it challenges a persistent assumption in AI: that openly licensed data inherently produces inferior models.

To test this, the team trained two 7B parameter models (Comma v0.1-1T and Comma v0.1-2T) on the Common Pile. The results? Models that perform comparably to leading systems trained on unlicensed data in the same parameter regime.

Through ablation studies, they found that:

  • ✅ Common Pile v0.1 outperforms models trained on other licensed datasets like KL3M, OLC, and Common Corpus
  • ✅ It performs comparably to ones trained on the original Pile or OSCAR
  • ⚖️ While there’s still a gap compared to FineWeb, this likely stems from FineWeb’s larger initial data pool allowing more aggressive quality filtering

As the pool of accessible openly licensed and public domain data grows, we can expect this gap to narrow even further.

🌱 Looking Forward: This Is Just the Beginning

The “v0.1” in Common Pile’s name signals the team’s commitment to continued improvement. Far from a one-off release, this represents the first step in building a comprehensive ecosystem of openly licensed training data.

EleutherAI and partners have already developed various tools, standards, and pipelines for data extraction and license identification. In June 2024, they collaborated with Mozilla on a Dataset Convening to establish best practices for open datasets in LLM training.

The team sees particular potential in partnerships with the cultural heritage sector. The current dataset already contains texts from nearly 300,000 public domain books digitized by the Library of Congress and Internet Archive. Applying modern OCR models like Docling or Surya could dramatically improve text quality for future releases.

🤔 A New Dawn for Open AI Development?

The Common Pile v0.1 arrives at a critical moment for AI transparency. As commercial entities retreat behind walls of secrecy, this project demonstrates that openness and high performance aren’t mutually exclusive.

For researchers, developers, and the broader AI community, this 8 TB corpus offers more than just training data—it provides a foundation for reproducible science, collaborative innovation, and accountable AI development.

The question now is: will more organizations follow this path toward transparency, or will the industry continue its slide toward opacity? The success of Comma models suggests that choosing openness needn’t come at the cost of performance.

item.title: Breaking Ethical Ground: Common Pile & Comma Models Prove You Don't Need to Steal Data
item.description:
🚀 Breaking Ethical Ground: Common Pile & Comma Models Prove You Don’t Need to Steal Data

📊 Summary

The Hugging Face team has released Common Pile v0.1, an 8TB dataset of legally sound, openly licensed text spanning 30 diverse sources. To prove its efficacy, they’ve trained two 7B parameter language models (Comma v0.1-1T and v0.1-2T) that compete with major models trained on questionable data. This breakthrough challenges the industry assumption that powerful AI requires ethically dubious training materials.

🌟 Ethical AI: No Longer Just a Dream

For years, the AI community has wrestled with an uncomfortable truth: many of the most powerful language models are trained on vast amounts of text scraped from the internet with little regard for copyright, licensing, or consent. The question lingering in researchers’ minds has been whether it’s even possible to build competitive models without resorting to these ethically questionable practices.

Today, we have our answer. And it’s a resounding “yes.” 🙌

The release of the Common Pile v0.1 dataset and accompanying Comma models represents a watershed moment in AI development. This project demonstrates that ethical considerations and technical excellence aren’t mutually exclusive—they can and should coexist.

🧠 What Makes the Common Pile Special?

Diverse, Legal, and Massive

The Common Pile isn’t just another dataset—it’s an 𝟴 𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗯𝘆𝘁𝗲 collection carefully curated from 30 distinct sources, all adhering to proper licensing. This diversity ensures models trained on it develop a rich understanding across multiple domains:

  • 📚 Books and literature
  • 💻 Programming code
  • 🔬 Research papers
  • 🎓 Educational materials
  • 🎙️ Audio transcripts
  • 📜 Governmental text
  • …and much more

The team behind Common Pile has prioritized legal and ethical sourcing, using only openly licensed and public domain text. This stands in stark contrast to many existing datasets that incorporate copyrighted materials without permission or proper attribution.

A Foundation for Ethical Models

The dataset wasn’t created merely as an academic exercise—it was designed with practical application in mind. The creators posed a fundamental question: “𝙄𝙨 𝙞𝙩 𝙥𝙤𝙨𝙨𝙞𝙗𝙡𝙚 𝙩𝙤 𝙩𝙧𝙖𝙞𝙣 𝙥𝙚𝙧𝙛𝙤𝙧𝙢𝙖𝙣𝙩 𝙡𝙖𝙣𝙜𝙪𝙖𝙜𝙚 𝙢𝙤𝙙𝙚𝙡𝙨 𝙬𝙞𝙩𝙝𝙤𝙪𝙩 𝙪𝙨𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙪𝙣𝙡𝙞𝙘𝙚𝙣𝙨𝙚𝙙 𝙩𝙚𝙭𝙩?”

🔥 The Comma Models: Proving the Concept

To answer their own question, the team trained two language models on the Common Pile:

  • Comma v0.1-1T: A 7B parameter model trained on 1 trillion tokens
  • Comma v0.1-2T: A 7B parameter model trained on 2 trillion tokens

The results? 🤯 Nothing short of revolutionary. These models achieve competitive performance compared to similar-sized models like Llama 1 and 2 7B—models trained on data of questionable provenance.

This achievement shatters the persistent myth that cutting ethical corners is necessary to build powerful AI systems. The Comma models demonstrate that with careful curation and proper engineering, ethically sourced data can produce results that rival or potentially exceed those of less scrupulous approaches.

Technical Details That Matter

The team didn’t just release the models—they’ve provided complete transparency into their process:

  • ✅ Full model checkpoints available for download
  • ✅ Access to the filtered and rebalanced dataset used for training
  • ✅ Open-source code for data preparation on GitHub
  • ✅ Comprehensive documentation in their research paper

This level of openness sets a new standard for the field, allowing others to build upon their work and potentially improve these ethical approaches further.

🌈 The Future of Ethical AI

The “v0.1” designation in the project’s name isn’t accidental—it’s a clear signal that this is just the beginning. The team views this release as the first step on a longer journey toward building a more ethical language model ecosystem.

What might future versions include? We might see:

  • Expanded datasets with even greater diversity
  • Improved filtering techniques to ensure higher quality
  • More sophisticated balancing methods to reduce biases
  • Models of various sizes to accommodate different use cases
  • Community contributions to enhance the dataset’s breadth and depth

This collaborative approach to ethical AI development could fundamentally transform how we think about building these systems, proving that the AI community doesn’t need to compromise on ethics to achieve technical excellence.

🤔 A Paradigm Shift in AI Development

The Common Pile and Comma models don’t just represent technical achievements—they represent a potential paradigm shift in how we approach AI development. By demonstrating that competitive models can be built using exclusively ethical data sources, the team has challenged the entire industry to reconsider its practices.

For too long, many have assumed that cutting corners on data ethics was the price of progress. The Comma models suggest otherwise: perhaps the truly advanced approach is one that respects copyright, licensing, and the fundamental principles of ethical data usage.

As AI becomes increasingly integrated into our daily lives, the methods used to create these systems matter more than ever. The Common Pile project offers a glimpse of a future where powerful AI and ethical considerations advance hand-in-hand.

💡 What’s Next?

If you’re intrigued by this project (and you should be!), there are several ways to engage:

  1. Explore the dataset and models firsthand
  2. Review their paper for detailed methodology and results
  3. Open an issue on GitHub if you have ideas for improvement
  4. Reach out directly to the team to collaborate

As we stand at this ethical crossroads in AI development, one question remains: will the industry follow this lead and embrace methods that respect both legal and ethical considerations, or will it continue down the path of “scrape first, ask questions later”? The answer may determine not just how our AI systems perform, but what values they ultimately embody.

item.description:
🚀 VS Code Revolution: How GitHub Copilot Is Going Open Source

Summary: VS Code is making a groundbreaking move by open-sourcing GitHub Copilot Chat components and integrating core AI capabilities directly into VS Code. This article explores what this means for developers, why Microsoft is making this strategic shift, and how you can prepare to take advantage of these powerful AI features when they arrive in 2025.

🌟 The Unexpected AI Evolution: VS Code’s Bold New Direction

In a stunning announcement that has reverberated across the developer community, the VS Code team revealed plans to transform their beloved editor into an “Open Source AI Editor.” 🤯 This isn’t just another feature update—it’s a fundamental shift in philosophy concerning how AI-powered development tools should be built, maintained, and evolved.

On May 19, 2025, through their official blog post “VS Code: Open Source AI Editor,” the team outlined their vision: GitHub Copilot Chat extension code will be open-sourced under the MIT license, with key AI components being thoughtfully refactored into VS Code’s core functionality.

Why does this matter? Because for many developers, AI coding assistants have become essential productivity tools—but they’ve largely existed as closed-source, premium add-ons. This move signals a future where AI assistance becomes as fundamental to coding as syntax highlighting or code completion.

📸 Imagine a screenshot showing the evolution of code editors from simple text editors to intelligent coding assistants

🧠 The Strategic Rationale: Why Open Source AI Now?

The VS Code team’s decision wasn’t made lightly. After all, GitHub Copilot has been tremendously successful as a premium offering. So what changed?

1. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗟𝗟𝗠 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗱𝘀𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗲 𝗛𝗮𝘀 𝗘𝘃𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗲𝗱

Large Language Models have matured significantly. The “secret sauce” of prompt engineering that once gave proprietary systems their edge has diminished in importance as models themselves have become more capable. The team recognized this shift makes now the perfect time to open the ecosystem.

2. 𝙐𝙨𝙚𝙧 𝙀𝙭𝙥𝙚𝙧𝙞𝙚𝙣𝙘𝙚 𝙋𝙖𝙩𝙩𝙚𝙧𝙣𝙨 𝙃𝙖𝙫𝙚 𝙎𝙩𝙖𝙗𝙞𝙡𝙞𝙯𝙚𝙙

Common patterns for effective AI-human interaction in coding environments have emerged. By open-sourcing these patterns, VS Code provides a stable foundation that the community can build upon, rather than having everyone reinvent the UI wheel.

3. 𝑇𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑠𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑒𝑛𝑐𝑦 & 𝑆𝑒𝑐𝑢𝑟𝑖𝑡𝑦 𝐷𝑒𝑚𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑠

As AI tools become more integrated into development workflows, questions about data collection and security vulnerabilities have intensified. Open-sourcing addresses these concerns head-on by allowing developers to see exactly what data is being collected and how it’s used. Security benefits too, as more eyes on the code means faster identification and remediation of potential vulnerabilities.

“𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘑𝘰𝘶𝘳𝘯𝘦𝘺 𝘧𝘳𝘰𝘮 𝘊𝘭𝘰𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘵𝘰 𝘖𝘱𝘦𝘯 𝘐𝘴 𝘈𝘣𝘰𝘶𝘵 𝘌𝘮𝘱𝘰𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘊𝘰𝘮𝘮𝘶𝘯𝘪𝘵𝘺”

🔧 Getting Ready: How to Prepare for the Open Source AI Revolution

Since these AI features will be integrated into VS Code itself rather than offered as a separate “open-source Copilot,” you’ll want to ensure you’re using the latest version of VS Code when these features roll out. Here’s a quick setup guide for different platforms:

🪟 Windows Setup:

  1. Download the installer from the official VS Code website (code.visualstudio.com)
  2. Run the installer and activate the “Add to PATH” option
  3. Consider enabling helpful context menu features like “Open with Code”

🍏 macOS Setup:

  1. Download the Universal .zip file from the official site
  2. Extract and drag Visual Studio Code.app to your Applications folder
  3. To enable terminal access, open VS Code, press Cmd+Shift+P, and type “Shell Command: Install ‘code’ command in PATH”

🐧 Linux Setup:

Options include:

  • For Debian-based systems: Download and install the .deb package
  • For RHEL/Fedora: Use the .rpm package
  • For various distributions: sudo snap install --classic code

📸 Visualize a simple setup diagram showing VS Code installation across different operating systems

The most important preparation step is staying informed. Keep an eye on the VS Code blog and release notes for announcements about when these AI features will be integrated. Regular updates will ensure you’re ready when they arrive.

🔮 The Implications: What This Means for the Developer Ecosystem

This shift isn’t just about making one product’s features freely available. It represents a fundamental transformation in how we think about AI-assisted development tools. By creating an open foundation for AI coding assistance, VS Code is enabling:

  1. 🧩 Specialized Domain Adaptations: Community contributors can tailor AI capabilities for specific languages, frameworks, or domains

  2. 📚 Enhanced Educational Tools: More accessible AI coding tools will revolutionize how programming is taught and learned

  3. 🛠️ Innovative Coding Workflows: New development paradigms will emerge as developers experiment with and extend these AI capabilities

  4. 🔍 Greater Transparency: Developers can inspect exactly how these tools work, building trust in AI-assisted development

The most exciting aspect is that this transformation puts the community at the center of AI-assisted development’s future. Rather than passive consumers of proprietary AI features, developers become active participants in shaping how these tools evolve.

🌐 Conclusion: A New Chapter in Development History

VS Code’s decision to open-source GitHub Copilot Chat components and integrate AI capabilities into its core represents more than just a feature announcement—it’s a philosophical statement about the future of development.

By applying the time-tested principles of open source to cutting-edge AI, VS Code is betting that community collaboration will produce better, more trustworthy AI coding tools than closed systems can. Given open source’s track record of success, this seems like a wise bet.

As developers, we now have the opportunity to shape this exciting future. When these changes roll out, will you simply use these new AI features, or will you contribute to building them?

What kind of AI-powered development environment do you want to create?
